questions.question: In which Staffordshire cathedral city was Dr. Samuel Johnson born in September 1709?
questions.explanation: Samuel Johnson was born on 18 September 1709 in Lichfield Staffordshire where his father Michael was a bookseller.

questions.question: What is the title of Samuel Johnson's only drama, a blank-verse neoclassical tragedy staged by David Garrick at Drury Lane in 1749?
questions.explanation: Johnson brought the manuscript of his tragedy Irene to London in 1737 and Garrick produced it in February 1749.

questions.question: Which 1749 philosophical poem in heroic couplets was the very first publication to bear Samuel Johnson's own name on its title page?
questions.explanation: Published in January 1749 The Vanity of Human Wishes was the first work to which Johnson attached his name.

questions.question: Which lighter weekly periodical essay series did Samuel Johnson contribute to 'The Universal Chronicle' between April 1758 and April 1760?
questions.explanation: Johnson wrote 91 of the 103 weekly issues of The Idler between 1758 and 1760 adopting a lighter conversational persona.

questions.question: In Samuel Johnson's 'The History of Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia' (1759), from what secluded paradise does the prince escape to survey the world?
questions.explanation: Rasselas grows restless amidst the effortless pleasures of the Happy Valley in Abyssinia and tunnels out with Imlac.

questions.question: In which year did Samuel Johnson finally publish his landmark eight-volume edition of 'The Plays of William Shakespeare'?
questions.explanation: Nine years after issuing his 1756 Proposals Johnson published his eight-volume edition of Shakespeare in October 1765.

questions.question: In his 'Preface to Shakespeare' (1765), while preserving the Unity of Action, which two neoclassical unities did Samuel Johnson famously reject?
options: The Unities of Meter and Diction
The Unities of Tragedy and Comedy
The Unities of Time and Place
The Unities of Character and Sentiment
questions.explanation: Johnson argued that spectators always know the stage is only a stage invalidating strict rules of time and place.

questions.question: With which celebrated portrait painter and first President of the Royal Academy did Samuel Johnson co-found 'The Club' in London in 1764?
questions.explanation: Reynolds proposed The Club in February 1764 to give Johnson an arena for his conversation at the Turk Head Tavern.

questions.question: Which 1775 travel book did Samuel Johnson publish recounting his autumn 1773 tour through the Scottish Highlands and islands with James Boswell?
options: The Journal of a Voyage to Lisbon
A Journey to the Western Islands of Scotland
A Tour Thro' the Whole Island of Great Britain
questions.explanation: Johnson published A Journey to the Western Islands of Scotland in January 1775 reflecting on Highland culture and clan life.

questions.question: Which 1764 philosophical poem in heroic couplets, subtitled 'A Prospect of Society', was the first work to bear Oliver Goldsmith's name?
questions.explanation: Published in December 1764 The Traveller surveyed European nations from the Alps and established Goldsmith poetic fame.

questions.question: Which five-act comedy featuring the overly generous Mr. Honeywood and the gloomy alarmist Croaker was Oliver Goldsmith's first staged play in 1768?
questions.explanation: George Colman produced Goldsmith first comedy The Good-Natur'd Man at Covent Garden in January 1768.

questions.question: In Oliver Goldsmith's 1773 comedy 'She Stoops to Conquer', which country squire's daughter poses as a barmaid to win the bashful Young Marlow?
questions.explanation: Learning that Marlow is tongue-tied before ladies of quality but bold with barmaids Kate Hardcastle stoops to conquer him.

questions.question: Which prank-loving stepson of Mr. Hardcastle in 'She Stoops to Conquer' tricks Marlow and Hastings into mistaking Hardcastle's manor for an inn?
questions.explanation: At the Three Pigeons alehouse Tony Lumpkin directs the London travellers to his stepfather house as the Buck Head Inn.

questions.question: In which 1773 essay published in 'The Westminster Magazine' did Oliver Goldsmith champion 'laughing comedy' over tearful 'sentimental comedy'?
options: An Inquiry into the Present State of Polite Learning
Preface to the Beauties of English Poesy
An Essay on the Theatre; or, A Comparison between Laughing and Sentimental Comedy
questions.explanation: Published just before She Stoops to Conquer in 1773 this essay attacked weeping comedies as a mulish bastard genre.

questions.question: Which 1777 comedy of manners by Richard Brinsley Sheridan contrasts the hypocritical, sententious Joseph Surface with his extravagant brother Charles?
questions.explanation: Staged at Drury Lane in May 1777 The School for Scandal exposes malicious gossip and the false morality of Joseph Surface.

questions.question: In Sheridan's 'The School for Scandal', which young country-bred wife is discovered hiding behind a screen in Joseph Surface's library?
questions.explanation: In the famous Screen Scene of Act IV Scene 3 Charles Surface knocks down the screen revealing Lady Teazle to Sir Peter.

questions.question: Which 1779 satirical afterpiece by Richard Brinsley Sheridan, subtitled 'A Tragedy Rehearsed', features the theatrical promoter Mr. Puff?
questions.explanation: The Critic or A Tragedy Rehearsed premiered in October 1779 updating the burlesque rehearsal format of Buckingham and Fielding.

questions.question: In Sheridan's 'The Rivals' (1775), under what penniless army ensign's name does Captain Jack Absolute court the romance-loving Lydia Languish at Bath?
questions.explanation: Because Lydia Languish wants to elope and lose her fortune for love Jack Absolute disguises himself as poor Ensign Beverley.

questions.question: Which seven-volume epistolary novel did Samuel Richardson publish in 1753–1754 to portray a model Christian gentleman of spotless honour?
options: The Adventures of Sir Launcelot Greaves
The History of Sir Charles Grandison
questions.explanation: Urged by female friends to create a good man to contrast with Robert Lovelace Richardson published Sir Charles Grandison in 1753-1754.

questions.question: Who is the spirited and virtuous daughter of Squire Western whom the hero loves throughout Henry Fielding's 1749 novel 'Tom Jones'?
questions.explanation: Modeled on Fielding beloved first wife Charlotte Cradock Sophia Western flees home rather than marry the hypocritical Blifil.

questions.question: Which 1751 domestic novel—Henry Fielding's final completed novel—portrays the patient, devoted wife of the improvident Captain William Booth?
questions.explanation: Published in December 1751 Amelia focuses on married life social injustice and the reform of Captain Booth through Amelia fidelity.

questions.question: Which poignant autobiographical work, published posthumously in 1755, records Henry Fielding's final sea journey to Portugal before his death?
options: The Journal of a Voyage to Lisbon
questions.explanation: Fielding sailed for Lisbon in June 1754 died there in October 1754 and his Journal appeared posthumously in February 1755.

questions.question: Which 1751 picaresque novel by Tobias Smollett features the memorable retired naval eccentric Commodore Hawser Trunnion?
questions.explanation: Smollett published Peregrine Pickle in 1751 depicting the hero upbringing near Commodore Trunnion fortified garrison house.

questions.question: In what narrative form is Tobias Smollett's 1771 comic novel 'The Expedition of Humphry Clinker' told as Matthew Bramble's party tours Britain?
options: A series of letters written by six different family members and servants
A set of dramatic dialogues recorded by a country parson
A continuous first-person prison confession by Humphry Clinker
questions.explanation: Humphry Clinker is an epistolary novel without replies presenting the same events through six contrasting epistolary voices.

questions.question: Which 1768 work by Laurence Sterne, narrated by Parson Yorick, popularized the genre of the sentimental travel narrative shortly before Sterne's death?
options: A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy
questions.explanation: Published in February 1768 just weeks before Sterne died A Sentimental Journey tracks Yorick emotional encounters in France.

questions.question: Which 1771 novel by the Scottish writer Henry Mackenzie portrays the sensitive hero Harley, who sheds tears of sympathy over every human woe?
questions.explanation: Henry Mackenzie published The Man of Feeling anonymously in 1771 creating the supreme archetype of the sentimental hero in Harley.

questions.question: Which 1752 satirical novel by Charlotte Lennox portrays the young heiress Arabella mistaking contemporary Georgian society for French heroic romances?
questions.explanation: In The Female Quixote or The Adventures of Arabella 1752 Arabella is cured of her romance delusions by a learned clergyman.

questions.question: Which 1749 work by Sarah Fielding, set at Mrs. Teachum's boarding school for nine girls, is regarded as the first full-length novel written for children?
options: The Governess; or, The Little Female Academy
The History of Sandford and Merton
The History of Little Goody Two-Shoes
questions.explanation: Sarah Fielding sister of Henry Fielding published The Governess in 1749 inaugurating the English school story for children.

questions.question: In Horace Walpole's 1764 Gothic novel 'The Castle of Otranto', who is the tyrannical usurping prince whose son Conrad is crushed by a giant helmet?
questions.explanation: Prince Manfred of Otranto attempts to divorce his wife Hippolita and marry Conrad betrothed Isabella after Conrad death.

questions.question: Which Gothic novel by Clara Reeve, first published in 1777 as 'The Champion of Virtue', sought to blend Walpole's Gothic romance with probable realism?
options: The Castles of Athlin and Dunbayne
questions.explanation: Clara Reeve retitled her novel The Old English Baron in 1778 calling it the literary offspring of The Castle of Otranto.

questions.question: Which decadent Oriental Gothic novel about the ninth Abbasid Caliph who builds a tower to reach heaven was written in French in 1782 by William Beckford?
questions.explanation: Beckford wrote Vathek in French in 1782 and Samuel Henley published an unauthorized English translation in 1786.

questions.question: What is the exact stanza form used throughout Thomas Gray's 1751 masterpiece 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard'?
options: Heroic quatrains of iambic pentameter rhyming abab
Closed heroic couplets in iambic pentameter
Spenserian nine-line stanzas ending with an alexandrine
questions.explanation: Gray composed all thirty-two stanzas of the Elegy in four-line iambic pentameter quatrains rhyming abab known as the elegiac stanza.

questions.question: Which witty mock-elegy did Thomas Gray compose in 1747 after Horace Walpole's pet cat Selima drowned in a Chinese porcelain tub?
options: Ode on the Death of a Favourite Cat, Drowned in a Tub of Gold Fishes
questions.explanation: Printed in Dodsley Collection in 1748 the poem ends with the famous moral Nor all that glisters gold.

questions.question: How did Thomas Gray respond in December 1757 when he was offered the post of Poet Laureate following the death of Colley Cibber?
options: He declined the appointment, which was then conferred upon William Whitehead
He resigned his Cambridge fellowship to serve at the court of George II
He accepted the post and held it until his death at Cambridge in 1771
He accepted the salary on condition that he write only Latin odes
questions.explanation: Gray scorned the degraded office of Poet Laureate and refused it though he later accepted the Regius Professorship of Modern History in 1768.

questions.question: Which short twelve-line patriotic lyric by William Collins opens with the famous lines 'How sleep the brave, who sink to rest, / By all their country's wishes blest!'?
options: The Passions: An Ode for Music
Ode Written in the Beginning of the Year 1746
questions.explanation: Written during the Jacobite uprising of 1745-1746 Collins twelve-line ode honors soldiers fallen in battle for their country.

questions.question: Which ecstatic eighty-six-stanza religious poem in six-line tail-rhyme stanzas did Christopher Smart publish in 1763 celebrating the biblical psalmist?
options: On the Eternity of the Supreme Being
questions.explanation: Published in April 1763 shortly after Smart release from Mr Potter madhouse A Song to David culminates in a glorious catalog of adoration.

questions.question: With which evangelical curate and former slave-ship captain did William Cowper collaborate to compose the famous 'Olney Hymns' published in 1779?
questions.explanation: Cowper contributed sixty-seven hymns and John Newton wrote the remainder including Amazing Grace for the 1779 Olney Hymns.

questions.question: Which wildly popular 1782 comic ballad by William Cowper narrates the runaway horseback ride of a London linen-draper to Edmonton and Ware?
options: The Diverting History of John Gilpin
On the Receipt of My Mother's Picture
questions.explanation: First printed anonymously in The Public Advertiser in November 1782 John Gilpin became a sensation across Britain.

questions.question: Which six-book meditative blank-verse poem did William Cowper publish in 1785, opening with a mock-Miltonic history of furniture titled 'The Sofa'?
questions.explanation: Cowper published The Task in six books in July 1785 bridging eighteenth-century didactic verse and Wordsworthian conversational blank verse.

questions.question: Which 1783 poem in heroic couplets by George Crabbe rejected the idyllic nostalgia of Goldsmith's 'Auburn' to portray the grim reality of rural poverty?
questions.explanation: Set on the bleak Suffolk coast near Aldeburgh Crabbe The Village 1783 declared that he would paint the cot As Truth will paint it and as Bards will not.

questions.question: Whose monumental six-volume 'The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire' began publication in London in February 1776?
questions.explanation: Edward Gibbon published Volume I in 1776 Volumes II and III in 1781 and the final three volumes in 1788.

questions.question: Published in March 1776, which foundational five-book treatise of classical economics was authored by the Scottish philosopher Adam Smith?
options: An Essay on the History of Civil Society
An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations
An Inquiry into the Principles of Political Oeconomy
questions.explanation: Adam Smith published The Wealth of Nations on 9 March 1776 analyzing the division of labour free markets and the invisible hand.

questions.question: Before writing 'The Wealth of Nations', which 1759 philosophical work did Adam Smith publish grounding morality in human sympathy and the 'impartial spectator'?
questions.explanation: Based on his Glasgow lectures Smith 1759 The Theory of Moral Sentiments provided the philosophical foundation for the culture of sensibility.

questions.question: Which Anglo-Irish statesman delivered the celebrated parliamentary speeches 'On American Taxation' (1774) and 'On Conciliation with the Colonies' (1775)?
questions.explanation: As MP for Bristol Edmund Burke argued in March 1775 that a great empire and little minds go ill together urging conciliation with America.

questions.question: Which wealthy literary hostess and critic, styled the 'Queen of the Blues', led the intellectual salon known as the Blue Stockings Society from the 1750s?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth Montagu hosted the Blue Stockings Society bringing together learned women and men for literary conversation instead of card-playing.

questions.question: Which legendary eighteenth-century actor-manager and former Lichfield pupil of Samuel Johnson revolutionized English acting at Drury Lane Theatre (1747–1776)?
questions.explanation: David Garrick walked to London with Samuel Johnson in 1737 triumphed as Richard III in 1741 and managed Drury Lane for twenty-nine years.

questions.question: Which 1761 satirical poem by Charles Churchill evaluated contemporary London stage actors and won overnight fame for its author?
questions.explanation: Named after the Roman actor Roscius Churchill 1761 satire The Rosciad mocked nearly every London player while awarding the chair to Garrick.

questions.question: Which Scottish philosopher and poet published 'The Minstrel; or, The Progress of Genius' (1771–1774) in Spenserian stanzas about the young shepherd Edwin?
questions.explanation: James Beattie published Book I of The Minstrel in 1771 and Book II in 1774 anticipating Wordsworth Prelude in tracing a poet growth in nature.

questions.question: Which mid-century poet and creator of the Leasowes landscape garden authored the affectionate Spenserian burlesque 'The School-Mistress'?
questions.explanation: William Shenstone published versions of The School-Mistress in 1737 1742 and 1748 portraying a village dame school in Spenserian stanzas.

questions.question: Which twentieth-century Canadian literary critic popularized the term 'Age of Sensibility' in his seminal 1956 essay 'Towards Defining an Age of Sensibility'?
questions.explanation: Northrop Frye published Towards Defining an Age of Sensibility in ELH in June 1956 establishing the period distinct literary identity.
